t1.endpoint_estimator: (last - first) / duration; an endpoint statistic that is blind to the path between the ends. On an evenly spaced series it equals the mean of the successive interval slopes, which is why the two agree exactly here
t1.least_squares_estimator: ordinary least squares of value on device_ms over the whole window (least_squares_slope_c_per_s); uses every row, so it follows the trend the row set actually has
t1.median_estimator: median of the per-interval slopes; the DS18B20 quantises at 0.0625 degC, so most 1 Hz intervals step by nothing and a median of 0 states that the box held frame to frame, not that it did not drift
t1.reading: the two gradient figures are different estimators of different questions and are published apart; quoting either one as 'the gradient' without naming the estimator and the window repeats the ambiguity docs/01 §20.5 forbids

window.definition: every row this layer accepted for thermal use, in source order, per slot
window.temperature_representation: the raw single-probe value of this slot; not a chamber-air mean and not Tmean

per_probe_noise.assumption: floor(H) = z * sigma_second_diff / sqrt(H), where sigma_second_diff is the trend-immune second-difference sigma (std of second differences / sqrt(6)) reported by probe_noise_profile(), and z is the stated detection z-score (default 2.58). The 1/sqrt(H) factor assumes white-noise residuals over the horizon; autocorrelated drift would make the floor larger, not smaller, so this is an optimistic bound
per_probe_noise.estimator: second-difference sigma (trend immune), pooled across accepted runs

t2.excluded_from_chamber_mean: TEC_HOT_SIDE is a heatsink, not chamber air

per_probe_noise.selection_rule: contiguous runs of snapshot=VALID AND state=OFF AND duty=0, then rejected if the fitted slope exceeds the threshold
